small_guidance:
- Switch to NHWC/channels-last layout for the conv input/output so the GEMM-K (IC) dimension is contiguous; this turns the strided per-channel gathers into coalesced loads and typically gives 1.5-2x on im2col conv kernels. Update x_ptrs/w_ptrs/out_ptrs strides accordingly.
- Add larger autotune tiles now that small ones are known to compile: `(BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=16, num_warps=8, stages=2)` and `(128, 64, 32, 8, 3)`. With KH=KW=3, IC_KHKW=576 — BLOCK_K=16 wastes K-loop iterations; try BLOCK_K=32 or 64 with stages=2 to verify SMEM fit (`(BM·BK+BK·BN)*4*2 ≲ 132KB`).
- Fuse the 2x2 maxpool + Mish epilogue into the conv kernel: have each program produce a BLOCK_N tile of pooled outputs by computing 2x2 conv outputs in registers and reducing, eliminating the conv_out write/read entirely (saves a full N·OC·OH·OW round-trip to HBM).
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a single fused kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, pooled-spatial tile). Inside, compute the 2x2 conv outputs needed for each pooled location (4 conv outputs per pooled output), apply -subv + hardswish, max-reduce to one value, then mish, and store. This eliminates the intermediate conv_out tensor (128·128·126·126·4B ≈ 1 GB of HBM traffic).
- Use channels-last (NHWC) input/weight layout so the K-loop over IC is the contiguous axis, enabling vectorized coalesced loads on the im2col gather. Pre-permute weight to (OC, KH, KW, IC) once in `__init__` (not at init-time reduction — this is a layout change only, same flops).
- Pick tiles aligned to pooled output: e.g. BLOCK_M=64 (OC), BLOCK_N=32 pooled spatial = 64 conv positions in a 2x2 pattern; BLOCK_K=64 over IC. Verify SMEM: `(64·64 + 64·128)·4·2 ≈ 96 KB` fits. Add an autotune over a few of these.
